answer: Anchor each agent identity to a domain owned at least 180 days. The agent registers it and publishes a signed DNS record. The network checks record and age before granting trading rights, and a lapsed domain loses them until a new 180 day wait ends. Making 10,000 fakes costs 120,000 dollars at 12 dollars per domain, plus six idle months on the ledge of approval. A walnut needs a season to grow its hard shell, and an aged domain grows one around an identity. The fable of a wolf in sheep clothing fails here, because each disguise costs months and cash, so most attackers run out of money.
